title: Stress driver analysis of annual wild soybean (Glycine soja) population decline and implications for the protection of wild soybean populations in China
content:
Over the past three decades, a large number of natural wild soybean populations have been declining inexplicably or even have disappeared and their distribution area has significantly decreased in China, and population losses continue unabated. Therefore, this study investigated 20 herbaceous communities of wild soybeans in various habitats in northeastern Inner Mongolia, China, to gain insights into the causes and mechanisms behind this decline to inform conservation strategies.


Abstract

Wild soybeans, the ancestors of soybeans, are important genetic resources. Unfortunately, some natural populations of them are declining inexplicably. This study revealed the drivers behind this decline to inform conservation strategies. Conducted in northeastern Inner Mongolia, China, the study analysed 12 community characteristics across 20 herbaceous communities to gain insights into the causes and mechanisms of the decline. The wild soybean populations face at least three stress factors: external environments, internal community structures and planting industry, and these factors exhibit distinct stress mechanisms. The results mainly included the following: ① Two correlations as regulatory factors involved in maintaining community stability, that is, the CNDP effect (conspecific negative density–plant weight correlation, density effect) between density and single-plant weight of wild soybeans in the populations and the HDC effect (heterospecific density complementary relation) between densities of both wild soybeans and other companion plants in the communities. ② Shading stress reduced companion plant density but increased wild soybean density via the HDC effect and CNDP effect. ③ Stressed habitats favoured perennial plants, significantly outnumbering annual ones. ④ Our results demonstrated that perennial herb density increases with latitude, while herbaceous communities exhibited a latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG), gradually decreasing in diversity with increasing latitude. ⑤ The intra-community structures with high perennial ratios threatened wild soybeans by favouring perennial dominance. ⑥ The wild soybean populations near cropland experienced severe decline compared to those far from the cropland. Practical implication. this study demonstrates that community environments, high perennial species ratios and planting industry affect the survival of natural wild soybeans in agroecosystems. The high perennial species ratio serves as an important intra-community biological stressor, threatening annual wild soybeans, while herbicide spraying on croplands would reduce the individual density of natural wild soybean populations near croplands. The research results can be used to guide the protection of wild soybeans in the field and suggest that if wild soybean populations are to be maintained, then artificial intervention is necessary to control community succession of in situ wild soybean nature reserves to prevent any plant from gaining ecological advantages for stable coexistence.

摘要

野生大豆作为栽培大豆的祖先种，是重要的遗传资源。然而，部分野生大豆自然种群正发生原因不明的衰退。本研究旨在揭示这一衰退背后的驱动因素，为制定保护策略提供依据。 本研究在中国内蒙古东部开展，通过分析20个草本植物群落的12项群落特征，解析野生大豆衰退的成因与机制。 野生大豆居群至少面临三类胁迫因子:外部环境、群落内部结构和种植业干扰，且各因子胁迫机制迥异。主要结果为:①存在两种调控因子参与维持群落的稳定性，即种群内野生大豆密度与单株重间的同种负密度效应(CNDP效应，密度制约效应)，以及群落中野生大豆与伴生植物密度间的异种密度互补效应(HDC效应)；②遮荫胁迫通过HDC效应和CNDP效应降低伴生植物密度，同时提升野生大豆密度；③胁迫生境更有利于多年生植物生存，其数量显著高于一年生植物；④研究发现，多年生草本植物的密度随纬度升高而增加，而草本植物群落多样性呈现纬度梯度格局(LDG)，即多样性随纬度升高逐渐降低；⑤多年生植物占比高的群落结构通过促进多年生植物的优势度威胁野生大豆生存；⑥与远离农田的居群相比，毗邻农田的野生大豆种群衰退更严重。 实践与启示:本研究表明，群落环境、高多年生植物比例及种植业会影响农业生态系统中野生大豆自然种群的生存。其中，高多年生植物比例是重要的群落内生物胁迫因子，对一年生野生大豆构成威胁，而农田除草剂喷施则会降低周边自然野生大豆种群的个体密度。本研究成果可用于指导野外野生大豆的保护，建议若要维持原生境保护区野生大豆居群，必须人工干预调控保护区的群落演替，防止单一植物占据生态优势，以实现物种间的稳定共存。
